Each `*Update` type has `ApplyTo(*types.T)` to project set and `SetNull`

`<Type>FilterConditions(filter, &args)` gives a filter's conditions, each

appended to `args`, their placeholders numbered after those already there.

`FindPage(ctx, filter, opts)` reads a page of the rows a filter finds, in a
`<Type>Sort`'s order of one column, ties broken by the primary key: one query
of `Limit + 1` rows after `After`, and no count. The page's `Next` is the
`<Type>PageKey` of its last row when more rows follow, which the next page
takes as `After`. A key is the row's primary key alone: the query reads the
key's row for its value of the sort's column, so an `After` whose row no
longer exists is `ErrPageKey`. A key does not say which order it came from,
so a cursor that carries one must name its sort, as a router's bound cursor
does. `Parse<Type>Sort` reads a page request's sort, `name` or `-name`, and
refuses a field the table cannot sort by. A page reads fastest with an index
on the sort's column, then the primary key, after any column the filter
compares by equality.

## Tables whose fields are behaviors

A table whose fields are behaviors (D103) stays a table: each field a
behavior owns is a column its row holds, which `<Type>Create`, its create
and upsert input, and `<Type>Update` leave out. Creates, updates, deletes
and each field's operations
(`db.Order.Status().Transition(ctx, id, params)`)
run through the behaviors' core in a transaction over `RulesLayout`, as
the context's user holding no permissions unless `WithBehaviorCaller` names
a caller. An upsert inserts a new row with what the core's create gives it,
and updates a row the key holds by its own fields alone. `UpdateMany` and
`DeleteMany` do not go through the core, and a table whose fields are
behaviors has no `UpdateOneIfVersion` or `DeleteOneIfVersion`: its version
is the fence every write through the core holds. A refusal of the core's is
a `*rules.Refusal`, and one of an operation on a key no live row holds wraps
`ErrNotFound` too. A raw SQL write of an owned column (`Tx.Exec`) is never
refused. The module requires `github.com/parable-work/superschematic/runtime/rules/go`,
which links the core's static archive through cgo: build it from a
superschematic checkout with `make rules-archive` (a `replace` directive to
that checkout finds it), or put a release's archives in `CGO_LDFLAGS` as
`-L<dir>/lib`.
